title: What does NFTokenModify do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of NFTokenModify and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, NFTokenModify changes the URI of an NFT that supports dynamic metadata updates. [1]

The DynamicNFT feature and token permissions constrain who can modify the token. Updating a URI changes the ledger's pointer, not necessarily the contents or availability of a remote resource. Check the precise token identifier and authority before signing. Buyers should distinguish an immutable token identity from metadata that its authorized party may change. [1]

The NFTokenModify reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using NFTokenModify, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
